spec.title: Migration from single-writer WAL and redbook composition

facts.INCOMPAT-WAL: `wal@1` requires one shared repository `WAL.xml` plus root `CONTINUE.md` to own personal session continuity. It is an alternative storage/authority model and must not be active with this flow.
facts.INCOMPAT-WAL-SPECSPACES: `wal-specspaces@1` multiplies that model by project root, not by contributor, branch or central session. It therefore remains single-writer within each specspace and must not be active with this flow.
facts.COMPAT-CAMPAIGN: `campaign-plans@1` is compatible when a repository campaign plan is a deliberately shared, integrator-owned contract. Its plan/ledger must not replace contributors' local adaptive plans, and non-integrators submit uniquely named records.
facts.COMPAT-MODES: `operating-modes@1` remains a session-scoped codeword system. Persistent interaction/planning settings in this flow are user preferences, not codewords and not permission to cross red lines.
facts.COMPAT-OTHER-REDBOOK: The remaining redbook@1 laws are compatible. Where an older document says “two writers” or puts WAL last in an authority chain, read “two or more writers” and “volatile local/shared projection” respectively; this flow supplies the N-writer coordination layer.

p.EDITION-LAW: A redbook version is an immutable tested roster. Do not mutate `redbook@1.0.0` and do not introduce environment-dependent variants under the same package version: identical coordinates must resolve to identical content. The eventual tested replacement is a later `redbook` edition (normally the next major if the continuity model is breaking), not a parallel `redbook-multiuser` brand.

p.TUNING-NOW: Before that edition exists, the existing resolver's per-edge deep `exclude` is the lawful consumer-side tuning mechanism. Exclusion narrows only the named dependency subtree and remains visible in the root manifest and lock/effective set.

p.DIRECT-EDGES: Remove any direct root edges to `wal` and `wal-specspaces`; an exclusion on the redbook edge cannot cancel an independent root path. After `vibe install --offline`, inspect `vibe.lock`, the effective package tree and generated boot lane: neither legacy boot snippet may remain.

facts.MIGRATE-INVENTORY: Inventory current `WAL.xml`, `CONTINUE.md`, root mode/planning files, specspace state, campaign plans, branch/worktree state and any unique reports. Do not delete first.
facts.MIGRATE-LOCAL: Create the matching `~/.vibe/steward` context. Preserve explicit owner settings (for example a root `mode = "auto"`) as context settings, construct the complete local plan, and mark unverified work candidate.
facts.MIGRATE-PROMOTE: Promote stable project facts and decisions out of volatile legacy files into their governing repository homes. Keep a shared campaign contract only when an integrator is named.
facts.MIGRATE-BOOT: Change manifest composition, regenerate offline, and replace repo boot text that mandates a personal WAL with the short multi-user-planning signpost. Keep harness entry files byte-identical when the project requires mirrors.
facts.MIGRATE-HANDOFF: Prove the new state with a real offer/receipt handoff to a fresh central session. The receiver must find the full route and every candidate without relying on chat history.
facts.MIGRATE-RETIRE: Only after receipt and project-fact promotion may legacy personal state be removed or archived. Cleanup is its own reviewed change.

p.SPECSPACE-TOPOLOGY: A repository may retain `SPECSPACES.md` as stable topology: name, root and boot contract. Remove personal defaults, current status and mutable session continuation from the shared registry. Each contributor's exact target/default and plan live in a local context.

p.TARGET-RESOLUTION: Resolve target by: explicit owner name or directory; unambiguous task/cwd inside a registered root; current local context; otherwise host project. Explicit always wins, unknown names are surfaced, and one session has one focus unless it announces a cross-project task.

p.BOOT-SCOPING: A targeted specspace session reads host-wide commit/safety rules plus the target's own boot and relevant specs; it does not load unrelated host/specspace plans. Continuity comes from the target-bound user-local context, not a specspace WAL.

p.MIXED-MODE-REFUSAL: If generated boot still loads this flow together with `wal` or `wal-specspaces`, do not choose whichever text appears later. Stop central state mutation, report the two competing continuity owners, and repair dependency composition. This is a configuration error, not a precedence puzzle.
